target.detail: the block, the bench, the same faces

setup: Bench by the shops, youngers on the bikes doing loops as eyes, the little bag taped under the bin. Routine as a milk round.
on_success: Steady traffic all shift, nothing above a twenty, no faces you don't know. Clean night on the block.
on_fail: One of the buyers is wearing shoes too clean for round here. He's not buying, he's counting. You clock it a beat too late.
on_crit: A wholesale face wants a proper amount and pays without a haggle. Double bubble, no bother.

target.name: the trap
target.detail: the flat with the reinforced door

setup: The flat above the offie, letterbox stuffed with foam, punters buzzing up all evening. Heat's up so keep it tight.
on_success: In-out on the buzzer, nothing on you longer than it takes to hand it over. Nerve held, block held.
on_fail: Buzzer goes and it's not a punter, it's a door coming off its hinges with a warrant behind it.
on_crit: A dry spell everywhere else means everyone comes to yours. You clear the lot at a premium.

target.detail: the bench by the shops, the same faces all evening

setup: Bench outside the offie, youngers doing loops on bikes as eyes, the little bag taped under the third slat. Regular as a milk round and about as exciting, which is exactly the point.
on_success: Steady traffic all shift, nothing above a twenty, no faces you don't already know. A clean night on a bench that's seen worse.
on_fail: One of the buyers has shoes too clean for round here. He's not buying, he's counting, and you clock it a beat too late.

target.name: Kyle
target.detail: the gap in the fence the sixth-formers use

setup: Lunchtime, a hole in the school railings worn smooth by years of it, and a queue of blazers with dinner money and bad ideas. You don't go to them; the gap brings them to you.
on_success: Ten minutes, twenty quid pieces, a line of kids who think they're getting away with something. Nobody's late back for double maths.
on_fail: A teacher on gate duty has been watching that fence for a term and today's the day she walks over instead of writing it down.
on_crit: One of them's spending his whole week's money and bringing his mates back for more. Repeat business starts young round here.

target.detail: the flat above the offie with foam in the letterbox

setup: Reinforced door, foam stuffed in the letterbox against a torch, punters buzzing up all evening. Heat's up in the ends so you keep it tight and you keep it moving.
on_success: In-out on the buzzer, nothing on you longer than it takes to pass it through the gap in the door. Nerve held, block held, night banked.
on_fail: The buzzer goes and it's not a punter — it's a door coming off its hinges with a warrant and a lot of shouting behind it.

target.detail: the 24-hour garage where cars pull in and don't buy petrol

setup: Night garage, bright as day, cameras everywhere, which is why nobody thinks you'd be daft enough. Cars pull onto the forecourt, a window goes down, a hand comes out, gone.
on_success: Six cars in an hour and not one of them bought fuel. The cashier inside has decided he sees nothing for a small consideration.
on_fail: The cashier's new and keen and he's already reading the number plates into a phone he thinks you can't see.

target.detail: the twelve-year-old on the BMX who does the actual handing over

setup: You hold nothing. A younger on a bike holds nothing either until a text sends him to a wall where nothing is taped. Three degrees of nothing between you and the corner. That's the whole design.
on_success: The kid does the loops, the punters get served, and if anyone gets stopped it's a child with an empty pocket and a good story.
on_fail: The kid gets pulled and he's twelve and scared and it turns out twelve-year-olds tell the truth faster than you'd hope.

target.name: Shanice
target.detail: the corner of a field where the phone signal dies

setup: Edge of a festival, past the last light, where a thousand people have money and no shop for a mile. No cameras out here, just torches and want and a field that swallows sound.
on_success: You could sell a week's worth in a night out here. They find you by word of mouth and pay whatever the dark decides is fair.
on_fail: Two of the torches coming towards you turn out to be event security who used to do exactly this and know every trick you've got.

target.detail: the whole ends gone quiet because everyone else got nicked

setup: A dry spell everywhere else means every phone in the postcode rings yours. Too much demand is its own kind of danger — a queue is a thing the police can see from space.
on_success: You ration it, keep the queue moving, and clear the lot at a premium nobody argues with. Scarcity does the pricing for you.
on_fail: The queue gets long enough to notice and long enough to film, and one of the faces in it has been sent to make exactly that happen.
on_crit: You're the only shop open in three postcodes. You've never counted this fast in your life.

target.detail: the community centre car park on the quiet afternoon

setup: Behind the community centre where the food bank runs, an afternoon lull, a low wall, and people who've learned to keep their heads down for reasons that have nothing to do with you.
on_success: A slow hour, small money, nobody looking. It's not glamorous and it barely covers the day, and some nights that's the whole job.
on_fail: A volunteer who does the food bank recognises somebody in your queue as their neighbour's kid and can't let it go.
